requirements.text: The kart is not faster than its set top speed.
requirements.design_point: Top speed on level paved ground, with the lightest and with the heaviest rider, is at most kart.speed_max_kmh.

requirements.text: The kart carries an adult.
requirements.design_point: Frame, axles, steering, seat, and their joints carry a rider of rider.mass_max_kg under the load cases of docs/03-design.md without yield or loosening.

requirements.text: The seat and pedals fit a child and an adult.
requirements.design_point: Without welding or cutting, the seat-to-pedal distance and the seat height adjust so that riders from rider.stature_min_cm to rider.stature_max_cm reach the pedals fully and hold the steering wheel with bent arms.

requirements.text: The kart runs on paved ground, gravel or dirt, and grass.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, on each of the three surfaces, the kart starts from rest, runs, turns, and stops, climbs site.grade_max_pct, and no part other than the tyres touches the ground.

requirements.text: The kart runs on packed snow and ice.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, on level packed snow, the kart starts from rest, runs, turns, and stops, at any speed.

requirements.text: The kart runs in fresh snow.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, on level fresh snow of depth snow.depth_max_cm, the kart starts from rest, runs, and turns at any speed without getting stuck.

requirements.text: The kart works in the cold.
requirements.design_point: After standing outdoors at ambient.temp_min_c, the kart starts and runs. With batteries it runs for kart.run_time_min per charge; with an engine it may be refuelled between runs.

requirements.text: The kart is built within the budget.
requirements.design_point: The parts list of docs/05-parts-and-cost.md, with tax, shipping, and winter parts, totals at most budget.parts_jpy, or the owner has accepted the excess.

requirements.text: The kart stops in a short distance.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, from kart.speed_max_kmh on level dry paved ground, the kart stops within kart.stop_distance_max_m.

requirements.text: The drive stops when the driver lets go.
requirements.design_point: The throttle returns to zero by a spring when released, and a stop switch that the driver reaches from the seat, and a helper reaches from beside the kart, cuts the drive.

requirements.text: Moving and hot parts cannot be touched.
requirements.design_point: Chain, sprockets, belt, the turning axle near the seat, and any hot part are covered so that the driver's hands, feet, hair, and clothing cannot reach them from the seat.

requirements.text: The kart slides before it tips over.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, half the track width divided by the height of the centre of mass is at least kart.tip_ratio_min on wheels and on skis with chains; in the snowmobile form, which runs only on snow, the distance from the centre of mass to the tipping edge divided by its height is at least kart.tip_ratio_snow_min.

requirements.text: The frame shields the driver's legs and feet.
requirements.design_point: Seen from the front and the sides, the driver's feet and legs are inside the frame or a bumper.

requirements.text: The kart is carried in a Mitsubishi Delica D:5.
requirements.design_point: With the rear seats of a Delica D:5 folded and slid forward, the kart passes through the tailgate opening (delica.opening_width_min_mm to delica.opening_width_max_mm wide) and lies within the cargo space (delica.cargo_length_mm long, delica.cargo_width_min_mm between the flipped-up third-row seats, delica.cargo_width_max_mm at most), after removing at most parts that come off without tools.

requirements.text: One adult loads and unloads the kart alone.
requirements.design_point: One adult rolls the kart up a ramp onto the cargo floor at delica.lip_height_mm and back down, without lifting the whole kart.

requirements.text: The kart climbs a fairly steep slope slowly without damage.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, on grass at site.grade_max_pct, the kart starts from rest on the slope and climbs at walking pace or faster, and no part slips, overheats, or deforms.

requirements.text: An adult can set a lower top speed for a small child.
requirements.design_point: Without tools, an adult sets the top speed on level paved ground to at most kart.speed_child_kmh, and the child cannot undo the setting from the seat.

requirements.text: The kart may be driven on public roads.
requirements.design_point: The kart meets every safety standard and registration rule that applies to its class of vehicle, listed from the law in step 1.1 (Q-021), and is registered with its number plate and compulsory insurance before it is driven on a road.

requirements.text: A belted driver is protected if the kart rolls over.
requirements.design_point: A roll bar rises above the head of the tallest driver (rider.stature_max_cm) seated, and carries the kart's weight upside down without collapsing onto the driver.

requirements.text: The kart has the lamps and reflectors of a moped.
requirements.design_point: A white head lamp that dips, a red tail lamp, a red stop lamp, a number plate lamp, a red rear reflector, and amber turn signals at the front and the rear on both sides, as P36 articles 62 to 64-3 ask.

requirements.text: The kart has two independent brake systems and a parking brake.
requirements.design_point: A foot brake on the rear wheels and a separate hand brake, either of which stops the kart, and a parking brake that holds it on law.parking_grade_pct (P36 article 61, P37).

requirements.text: The driver's seat has a seat belt and a head restraint.
requirements.design_point: A seat belt with anchors on the frame and a head restraint behind the driver's head, as P36 articles 66-2 and 66-3 ask for a seat that is not straddled.

requirements.text: The kart has a mirror, a horn, a speedometer, and an approved silencer.
requirements.design_point: An adjustable mirror on each side, a horn, a lit speedometer with an odometer in the driver's view, and the engine's own approved silencer (P36 articles 64, 64-2, 65, 65-2).

requirements.text: Other road users can see the low kart.
requirements.design_point: A structure at least law.marker_height_mm above the ground (P36 article 61-2), which the roll bar provides.

requirements.text: The kart is within the size of a moped.
requirements.design_point: Overall length at most law.length_max_mm and width at most law.width_max_mm (P36 article 59).

requirements.text: The engine is within the moped limit.
requirements.design_point: Displacement at most law.minicar_cc_max (P35).

requirements.text: The kart goes into calm water from a shore, floats and moves on it, and drives out again.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, in calm fresh water, the kart floats upright with a freeboard of at least water.freeboard_min_mm, moves at water.speed_min_kmh or more and steers, and drives out up a shore of water.shore_grade_pct.

requirements.text: The kart changes between a summer form on tyres and a winter form on skis and a track.
requirements.design_point: Two people change the kart from one form to the other with hand tools in at most kart.swap_time_h, without cutting or welding.

requirements.text: A driver whose kart capsizes or swamps in water, or breaks through ice, gets free and stays afloat.
requirements.design_point: On ice and near water the driver wears a life jacket and no seat belt, and nothing of the kart holds a driver in it when it rolls or goes through the ice - the driver gets out sideways under the roll bar without help. The kart itself need not float.

decisions.what: Build one go-kart with one seat, for the owner's private land, to be driven mainly by a child and also by an adult, in summer and in winter. The power source is not preset; the form step compares an engine and an electric drive.

Keep the record public in fujisato-koji/kart, created from the traceable-design template. The record is written in English and the conversation with the assistant is in Japanese. Private facts such as the place stay outside the repository.
The top speed is set for a child, at 30 km/h.
The speed is set for a child, but the strength and the seat and pedal positions must also fit an adult.
The kart runs only on private land, on paved ground, gravel or dirt, and grass. It does not run on public roads.
In winter the kart runs on private land on packed snow or ice and on fresh snow up to 30 cm deep.
The lowest air temperature in use is -10 degC.

The budget for parts and materials is 100,000 JPY, including tax, shipping, and the winter parts, and excluding tools. It is a guideline that may be passed a little; when it is likely to be passed, the assistant names the parts that drive it and the owner decides. The owner would buy a welder if the chosen form needs one.
The heaviest adult who drives weighs 100 kg.
The youngest driver is a 5-year-old child.
On snow the kart may be slow. The top speed of 30 km/h applies on paved ground.
The kart is kept outdoors under a roof, and is carried in a Mitsubishi Delica D:5, in which it should be easy to load and carry.
With an engine, refuelling between runs is acceptable. With batteries, two to three hours of driving per charge is wanted, depending on the trade-off.
The kart must not be damaged on a fairly steep slope. It may climb slowly.
The top speed on paved ground is lowered to 20 km/h, to see whether the kart can be made cheaper.
The tallest adult who drives is about 170 cm tall.

Make the design concrete with new parts that are readily available in Japan, with realistic shapes, and show the designed kart in 3D to grasp what will be built; the 3D view need not be a driving game. This settles item 1 of docs/02-form.md#proposal as new parts (L2). The other items of that proposal are taken as the working basis of step 1.3 until the owner decides them.
No lower speed limit for the child is needed; the kart has one top speed for every driver.
options: an adult sets a lower top speed for the child (R-17)
one top speed for every driver

decisions.what: The kart should also be driven on public roads, for short trips and leisurely runs near home in daytime, so it is to be equipped and registered as the law requires (most likely as a four-wheel moped, a minicar). The child drives only on private land. This changes D-005, which kept the kart off public roads.
The top speed is about 30 km/h, on public roads and on private land alike (one top speed, D-018). This replaces the 20 km/h of D-015.
options: fast on roads and slow on private land, switched

decisions.what: Road use comes first. The slope the kart must climb is lowered to what the engine allowed on public roads can do, instead of choosing a larger engine for the slope.

Reflect the proposal of docs/02-form.md#road in the design and the 3D view. The working basis becomes a used 50 cc four-stroke scooter engine with its CVT, centrifugal clutch, and final reduction in one unit, driving the rear axle by one chain; a roll bar over the driver's head that also serves as the 1 m marker; and the equipment the law asks for road use. The owner may still change the engine choice.

The kart is to be a personal vehicle for the far outdoors, in the owner's words like a kick scooter for the far outdoors. In winter it is changed into a snowmobile form - two front skis, one rear rubber track, and a sled bottom - to cross fresh snow that may lie about 1 m deep where nobody clears it, and in summer it is changed back to tyres for roads and private land. Aim at fresh snow 1 m deep and confirm it by the snowshoe test of Q-012. This raises the 30 cm of D-006 and starts a new pass of step 1.2.
options: fresh snow up to 30 cm with skis and chains or a pair of tracks (D-006)
a snowmobile form changed each winter, aiming at 1 m of fresh snow

decisions.what: The owner would like the kart, if it can be done, to drive from a shore straight into a lake, move on as a boat, and drive out again. Step 1.2 finds what that takes and what it costs before the owner confirms it.

Settles items 1, 2, and 5 of docs/02-form.md#outdoor. The winter form is the snowmobile form W3, driven by the summer 50 cc scooter unit (D1). R-12 is relaxed for the snowmobile form only, which runs only on snow - its tipping ratio need be at least kart.tip_ratio_snow_min, above the snow's grip. Item 3 (water) waits until the owner has heard what a ship inspection involves.
options: W3 the snowmobile form, or W1 kept for packed snow only
D1 the summer engine, or D2 the donor's engine in winter
R-12 relaxed for the snowmobile form, or the full margin on every setup

decisions.what: The driver may sit or stand, but if standing would keep the kart off public roads, the kart is ridden seated. A minicar needs a seat with a seat belt and a head restraint (R-22), so the kart stays seated. This settles Q-026.

Settles item 3 of docs/02-form.md#outdoor. The water requirement R-27 is withdrawn. Water use is kept only as a future development, shown in the 3D view as an option (side floats and an electric outboard on the tub) without a requirement; the tub stays for the snow and as safety buoyancy (R-29). Q-028 is closed until such a version is taken up.
options: the tub floats only for safety, and the owner asks the transport bureau before any boat use
R-27 withdrawn, the tub kept for snow and safety
boat use on an inspection pursued now, with side floats

decisions.what: R-29 keeps only the driver's safety - on ice and near water a life jacket and no seat belt, and nothing of the kart holding the driver. The kart need not float. This settles Q-030; the sled pan keeps its bottom strips and bow and loses its foam and the right pod, which were there only to float the kart.
options: the kart carries floats in winter so that it floats too

open.text: How heavy is the heaviest adult who will drive? The strength is assumed for 100 kg until the owner answers.

How tall is the tallest adult who will drive? The youngest is a 5-year-old (D-010); the lower end of the seat and pedal range is set from the statistics of 5-year-olds. The upper end is assumed at 185 cm until the owner answers.
Does the top speed of 30 km/h have to be reached on snow, or is a lower speed enough on packed snow and in fresh snow? R-05 and R-06 ask only that the kart runs, turns, and stops on snow.
Set the longest stopping distance from the top speed from a go-kart standard or kart rules. Until then it is assumed at 6 m, about 0.6 g.

Set the smallest ratio of half the track width to the height of the centre of mass, so that the kart slides before it tips, from tyre friction data and any standard. Until then it is assumed at 1.5. Also decide whether R-12 must hold standing sideways on site.grade_max_pct, which needs a wider track (form.track_min_slope_m, check K-001).
Where is the kart kept (indoors, under a roof, outdoors), and must it be carried in a car or a truck? This sets the size and mass limits and whether it stands in the cold before a run.
How often is the kart used, and by when should it be ready? The run time is settled by D-013.
How steep is the fairly steep slope of D-014? It is assumed at 20 % (about 11 degrees); D-021 lowers it to what the road-legal engine can climb, which is set when the engine is chosen.

The rough inputs of step 1.2 (kart mass and its rear share, tyre pressure, track wheel diameter, ski size, drive efficiency, tube lengths, ground clearance, heights of the centres of mass, and a mean speed, rolling resistance, electric efficiency, and usable battery fraction for the run time) are assumed so that forms can be compared. Step 1.3 replaces each with the chosen part's data or a calculation.

The price of the 12 V chargers for E2 and the allowances for shipping, small parts, a reduction stage, skis, the track running gear, pedals and cables and the stop switch, guards and mounts, drive chains, and electric wiring are assumed. Whether the snow chain price of M15 is for one tyre or a pair is not known; two are counted. Step 1.5 replaces each with a quoted price.

What is the governed no-load speed of the chosen engine? The gearing for R-01 is set to it. It is assumed at 3850 rpm from a checker's recollection (K-001), not from a source; take it from the engine maker's data, or measure it on the engine when it arrives.

How far does the owner's fresh snow give under a loaded plate? A board of known area loaded to about 5 kPa and to about 16 kPa, set on undisturbed fresh snow and its sinkage measured, settles whether rear tracks (W2) clear snow.depth_max_cm before the frame is given mounts for them. A person on snowshoes presses about 3.5 kPa (S4), the same order as a sled bottom (D-023), so the depth a snowshoe sinks in the deepest fresh snow is a first measure of whether the snowmobile form floats.

Should an adult be able to set a lower top speed for a small child? A 5-year-old drives (D-010), while US youth ATV guidance allows no ATVs under 6 and limits ages 6 and up to 10 mph with the restrictor (P25, S2). The child limit is assumed at 16 km/h, about 10 mph, until the owner decides R-17.

The 3D simulator needs the tyre grip on pavement, gravel, and grass, the sideways grip of the front skis, the resistance of tracks in fresh snow, and the resistance when the floor ploughs snow. No source was found; they are assumed so that the simulator can run, and a test run of the built kart settles them. Simulator results that rest on them are illustrations, not verification.

In the owner's Delica D:5, with the third row flipped up and the second row tipped up and slid forward, how wide is the clear space at the floor and at 40 cm above it, and how wide is the tailgate opening at the height of the cargo floor? The sources give only the narrowest and widest widths.
How many hours a day can the owner work on the kart? The plan in docs/data/plan.yaml assumes two to three hours a day for its task lengths.

Step 1.3 assumes, without a source yet, the dynamic load factor on the frame and axle, the density and strength of S45C and STKM11A steel, the masses of a wheel with its tyre, the clutch, the seat, the steering, the brake, the fuel, and small parts, the brake pad friction, and the ratio of buttock-to-heel length to stature for an adult and for a 5-year-old. Cite a standard, a maker's data, or a weighing for each before the gate from design to build.

The parts list assumes the price of steel plate cut to size, of machining by a local shop (keyways on the axle and the jackshaft, boring the 36 tooth sprocket, cross holes for the hub pins, the brake disc carrier), of making the two rear hubs, and of a 25 mm axle shaft of 1.22 m. Get quotes before the gate from design to build.

The fit of bought parts to each other is not stated by their sellers and is checked when they arrive, before the frame is welded to them - the rim's three-hole pattern against the front hubs and the made rear hubs, the front hubs' bore against the 17 mm spindles, the engine's shaft (3/4 inch Q-type) and base holes, and the seat's rail bolt spacing.

The layout of step 1.3 is not yet buildable (K-005). Rearrange the drive so that the chains, the jackshaft and its bearings, the middle axle bearing, and the guard fit between the seat and the left rail, or move the drive outboard; redesign the column support so it holds the column at its lower flange bearing and clears the legs; route the pedal box rails clear of the cross members; raise the steering arms and tie rods clear of the front rails; join every plate, the floor, and the seat slide to the frame; widen the seat space; and add the cornering side force to the axle and the engine's offset to the left rail.

Which class of vehicle the kart becomes on public roads (most likely a minicar, a four-wheel first-class moped with up to 50 cc or 0.6 kW rated electric output), and which safety standards (brakes, lamps, turn signals, mirrors, horn, speedometer, plate, size), registration steps, tax, and insurance apply; list each as a requirement with its article from the law.

How does the owner's municipality register a minicar built from scratch - how is a frame number given to a home-made frame, and which papers prove the engine's displacement (the donor's scrapping certificate, a receipt or transfer certificate, an engine-number rubbing)? No official page found covers a scratch-built frame; the owner asks the municipality's light vehicle tax counter.

The size and mass of a 50 cc scooter's engine and transmission unit, its final reduction, and its ECU's rev limit are not stated in any source found; the design assumes them. Measure the donor unit when it arrives, and set the drive sprockets so the top speed at the rev limit is kart.speed_max_kmh.

No seat belt marked JIS D4604, which the safety standards accept (P36 article 66-2), was found for sale to individuals; generic belts (M78) are not marked. A belt with its anchors from a scrapped kei car carries its approval; find one and its price, and check how it mounts on the kart's frame and seat.

The road-going layout is not yet buildable (K-006). Move the left side bar and the column braces clear of the scooter unit and the adult's shins; give the unit a plate on both rails; keep the axle sprocket and chain clear of the middle bearing plate; raise the roll bar above the tallest driver's head with a folding or bolted top for the car, with a front structure for a rollover; mount the hand brake, belt anchors, head restraint, battery, horn, and mirrors (facing the driver) on the frame; place the fuel tank, ECU, regulator, key switch, and the donor's silencer; add the cornering load to the axle and check a 30 mm axle; and carry the engine unit's mass on both rails. Build the collision search into calc/design.py so each change is checked.

The owner described the kart as like a kick scooter for the far outdoors (D-023). Does that ask for a standing ride, or for a light personal vehicle that is still seated? A standing ride conflicts with the seat, seat belt, and head restraint the law asks of a minicar on roads (R-22), and with a child driving.

The rough inputs of the snowmobile form and the hull - the track's place and mass (its size is a Yamaha Bravo's, P51), the parts removed and added at each change, the drive sprocket, the hull's size, foam share, and plating, the water design points, the outboard's battery, and the change time - are assumed until a donor is chosen and the hull is laid out in step 1.3.

A kart that moves on a lake is an amphibious vessel, a special ship, which the small-boat exemption from ship inspection does not cover (P46). Ask the regional transport bureau whether a home-built amphibious kart moved on water only by an electric outboard under 1.5 kW, with its engine stopped, can be inspected; whether a tub that the persons formula rates for nobody may be approved on an inclining test, or needs side floats for water days; whether the 50 cc engine counts as propulsion because it can turn the wheels in water; and whether a pond on private land is outside the Ship Safety Act (only named waters are exempt from registration, P58). What an inspection asks and costs is in docs/02-form.md#water (P55, P56). No official page on a small amphibious vessel was found.

The donor's track unit is drawn from assumed sizes - the track's thickness with its lugs, the rear idler's diameter, the drive shaft's height and its place ahead of the slide rails - which set the winter lift. Measure them on the donor (a Yamaha Bravo class) when it is bought, with its mass and mounting points, and check that a pivot shaft through the pillow blocks and brackets hanging from the rails can hold it.

The sled pan held 0.020 m3 of foam, which floated 0.15 of the winter kart's own weight, while R-29 asked water.reserve_ratio, which needed about 0.158 m3. The room is not there without bolting large floats on. With boat use withdrawn (D-027), should R-29 keep only the driver's part (a life jacket and no seat belt on ice, nothing holding the driver) and drop the kart's floating, or should the kart carry floats in winter?

checks.detail: An independent helper recomputed every claim by hand and then read calc/form_rough.py; the arithmetic held, the method did not in places. Found (1) P1's pmax is the contact pressure, not the inflation pressure, which does not change the conclusion; the sinkage exceeds the tyre radius, and the lowest part is the axle hardware, not the floor. (2) Tracks without road wheels carry the load under the sprocket and idler, so the even-belt pressure understates their sinkage; W2 passing R-06 was not shown, and P1 excludes tracked vehicles. (3) The climb needs rolling resistance on grass and gravel; a motor's force is limited by its controller current; 3600 rpm is P4's rated speed, not the governed no-load speed, so gearing to it may break R-01. (4) Whole teeth and tooth tips put the single-stage sprocket lower still. (5) The track width was rounded down, and R-12 on level ground does not cover the slope sideways. (6) Pedals, cables, stop switch, drive chains, guards, mounts, and electric wiring were missing from the cost, and two snow chains may be counted where one pair was priced. The script and record were changed on each point on the same day; see docs/02-form.md.

A second independent helper rechecked the repairs of K-001 by hand; all seven figures reproduce, and the script matches the record. Partial on the motors - the 2 kW kit's torque, speed, and current disagree (its rated current is probably the controller's rating), the text wrongly said the electric kits climb on pavement, and whether the controllers limit battery or motor current is not assessed. Also noted - the track wheel relation is used beyond its small-sinkage range, tracks on smaller wheels lower the rear axle, E1h has the same margin as E1, and the gearing limits speed only on level ground and uphill. The text of docs/02-form.md was corrected on each point the same day; no number changed.

A third independent helper recomputed the claims after the owner's second answers; every number matched its formula. Partial on what the text claimed - the climb was not checked for grip; the clutch's engagement and lock-up speeds came from two different clutches; a low child limit keeps a centrifugal clutch slipping; climbing at the lock speed is not slow; the overall width exceeded the widest opening only by rounding, and the narrowest opening was in the record but not cited; the battery margin is small; and the donor route left out a new wide axle and brake and treated the donor's ungoverned engine as E1. The record, calc/form_rough.py, and docs/02-form.md were changed on each point the same day; the simulator (with load transfer and rear-wheel spin) shows grip limiting the climb on grass.

An independent helper recomputed step 1.3 and searched docs/data/design.json for parts that collide. The arithmetic held, but the layout could not be built - the rear axle passed through the main rails and the axle cross member, the outer bearings were not joined to the frame, the seat sat on the drive and the brake, sprockets pierced the floor, the left side bar passed through the engine, the front tyre touched a side bar at full lock, the adult pedals lay inside the front cross member, and the hubs could not reach the transport track. Also the chains were rounded up and slack, the axle case left out the chain pull, the rail case was unfair, the sideways offset of the centre of mass and the downhill stop were left out, the transport width ignored the axle ends, and the text put the engine on the wrong side. calc/design.py, the design values, and docs/03-design.md were changed on each point the same day; the repairs wait for a re-check.

A second independent helper re-checked the repairs of K-004. The rear rails now clear the axle, the seat and the rider clear the drive and the brake, the floor clears the sprockets, the chains are whole even links, and the load cases reproduce. Still not buildable - between the seat and the left rail there is no room for both chains, the jackshaft and its bearings, the middle axle bearing, and the guard, which overlap by up to about 10 mm; the column support runs through the column and the adult's shins; the pedal box rail runs through two cross members, so it cannot slide to the child position; the steering arms and tie rod ends touch the front rails; the middle bearing plate, the jackshaft plate, the floor, and the seat slide are joined to nothing, and the outer bearing plates miss the outriggers by 3 mm. Also the left rail carrying the overhung engine is at a safety factor of about 1.3, the cornering side force on the axle is not yet a load case, and the downhill stop is about 19 m with the braking load shift. These are left open in Q-020 for the next design pass.

A third independent helper checked the road-going design of D-022. The arithmetic reproduces, but the layout cannot be built - the left side bar, a column brace, and the rising left rail pass through the scooter unit; the axle sprocket and chain pass through the middle bearing plate; the guard is cut by the axle; the roll bar is no higher than a 170 cm adult's head, and a bar that clears it does not fit the Delica unless it folds; the rear turn signals and mirror stems collide with the braces; the mirrors face backward behind the eyes; the horn passes through a cross member and the battery through the seat; the hand-brake caliper and lever, the belt anchors, the head restraint, and several plates are joined to nothing; the fuel tank, ECU, regulator, and key switch are not placed; the silencer is placed where the donor's may not fit. The roll bar's mass was counted at the wrong tube size, corrected the same day. The 25 mm axle is marginal under a cornering load and the left rail carries the engine unit at a safety factor of about 1.2. The rest is open in Q-025.

An independent helper recomputed every value of 1.2.14 and 1.2.15 by hand and checked the physics, the sources, and the comparisons in the text. The first round found five faults, all fixed the same day and passed on a second round - the foam was sized for the summer kart and is now sized for the heavier winter form; the outboard's battery was missing, which brings the tub's load rating just under the heaviest rider; P50 does not bar tracks for a moped and the text now says so; the kids' tracks and the smallest adult snowmobile lacked a source (S7 added, the claim limited to the listings); and the skipping speed was overstated as far beyond the top speed. The rear share ignores the skis and tub (about 0.71, not 0.73), within rough accuracy.

An independent helper checked the persons formula against the text of articles 102 and 103 of the Small Vessel Safety Rules (P55) and recomputed it by hand - index 0.607 (0.822 by the second formula), so nobody, and one person first at a beam of 1,160 mm. Taking the stern freeboard equal to the freeboard amidships is right for a level box; whether other articles limit the persons of a small boat was not checked.

An independent helper recomputed the winter form of 1.3.12 by hand and searched docs/data/design.json for interferences in the lifted winter form, in two rounds. The first found two errors (a bow of two panels called three; foam counted twice under the pod) and six interferences - the winter chain through the left pan strip and a cross member, hanging brackets through the pan and the floor, the slide rails' arms through the track's upper run, and a drive shaft too short. The design was changed - a wider tunnel, the cross member moved to 0.55 m, side plates beside the track carrying cross shafts inside the loop, the edge to the ski's outer corner, the belly counted with the track, stanchions and a chain guard added. The second round found all fixed but two new faults, the rear lugs drawn with the lift counted twice and the calipers through the right side plate; the assistant fixed both and checked the clearances from design.json (7 mm each). Clearances under 10 mm remain at the bow, the horn, the side plates' tops, and the chain to the left plate. The winter chain's 96 links sit at the boundary of the length formula. sm.removed_kg of 1.2 is not used by the design.

steps.action: Check the tyres for damage and their pressure.
Check that the chain and axle guards are on and the chains are tight.
Push the kart and press the brake pedal; the rear wheels must lock.
Work the throttle pedal; it must spring back to idle on its own.
Test both stop switches, the one on the steering and the tether.
Set the seat and the pedals for the driver with their pins.
Check that the driver wears a full-face helmet with long hair inside it, and no scarf.
Clear the driving area of people, vehicles, and objects.
An adult starts the engine outdoors with the recoil starter, the kart held by its brake.
The driver sits, clips the tether to the clothing, and holds the steering wheel.
Drive on level ground first; keep to kart.speed_max_kmh, or the child limit.
Climb and descend slopes straight, at full throttle uphill and at walking pace downhill; never turn across a slope.
To stop on a slope, use the brake, not the throttle.
In winter, drive slowly and brake early on snow and ice.
Stop the engine with the stop switch and let it cool.
Refuel outdoors, with the engine stopped and cool, away from children and flames.
Never run or warm up the engine in a closed shed.
On level ground, lift the kart onto four stands at the winter height, with the engine stopped and cold.
Take off the summer chain, the rear wheels with their hubs, the axle sprocket, the brake disc with both calipers, and the rear axle.
Slide the track unit's pivot shaft through the three pillow blocks, and bolt its drive shaft's bearings to the brackets under the rails.
Fit the brake disc and both calipers on the drive shaft, bleed nothing, and check that the brake holds.
Fit the 30T sprocket and the winter chain, tension it, and refit the chain guard.
Take off the front wheels and bolt the skis with their stanchions onto the spindles.
Lower the kart, check that the steering moves freely from lock to lock and that the track turns freely with the rear lifted.
Fold the third row up and tip and slide the second row forward.
Pull the pins, slide the rear hubs inward to the transport track, and pin them.
Hook the ramps on the cargo floor lip.
Push the kart up the ramps, with the engine stopped and the fuel tap closed.
Tie the kart down at the frame with two straps.
